user_saw: A read of a missing file in a very large directory could stall the Gateway main thread for a few hundred milliseconds while it computed filename suggestions.
summary: Made the read tool's missing-file suggestions pass the distance cutoff into the shared bounded Levenshtein helper, skip impossible lengths, and trimmed per-cell guards and row-minimum rescans in that helper.
reasoning: This is a performance optimization of a linear suggestion scan that the PR does not show was ever faster; results are identical before and after. Blame candidates are a refactor that added the bounded helper (32379ad) and a row-reuse perf change (c09eda8), neither of which made the read path slower, so there is no regressing commit and no functional failure.
